summary:
We developed the Wildfire Harmonization App, an interactive Streamlit web application that unifies active fire detection data from NASA’s MODIS (Collection 6.1) and VIIRS (S-NPP and NOAA-20) satellites for India. The app automatically downloads, cleans, standardizes, and merges multi-sensor FIRMS data into a single consistent dataset, solving the problem of fragmented satellite fire records that differ in resolution, format, detection algorithms, and confidence levels.
Users can explore the harmonized data through an interactive map, a fire-activity calendar that reveals seasonal patterns, time-series charts, and flexible filters by date, sensor, and confidence. The entire workflow is designed to be beginner-friendly, requiring no advanced GIS expertise.This project addresses a real challenge faced by researchers, students, and decision-makers: NASA provides powerful free fire data, but combining and analyzing it across sensors is time-consuming and technically complex. Our solution removes these barriers by delivering a ready-to-use, visual platform that makes Earth observation data more accessible and actionable.
The intended impact is to support better understanding of wildfire patterns in India, encourage wider use of NASA open data, and provide a lightweight, open-source tool that others can adapt for different regions. Built entirely with free tools, the app demonstrates how open data and simple technology can create meaningful solutions for environmental monitoring.
details:
Our project is a Wildfire Harmonization App that combines active fire data from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellites (S-NPP and NOAA-20) into one clean, easy-to-use platform focused on India.

Users download the free CSV files from NASA FIRMS, place them in the app, and the system automatically:

  1. Cleans and standardizes the different sensor formats
  2. Merges them into a single harmonized dataset
  3. Displays the results through an interactive Streamlit web dashboard

We want to lower the barrier to using NASA Earth observation data for wildfire monitoring in India and similar regions. By making multi-sensor fire data easy to explore, the app can support better awareness, research, and early planning for fire management agencies, researchers, and local communities.

  • Language: Python 3.10
  • Libraries: Streamlit, Pandas, GeoPandas, Folium, streamlit-folium, Plotly, NumPy
  • Data Source: NASA FIRMS Archive (MODIS C6.1 + VIIRS S-NPP + VIIRS NOAA-20)
  • Development environment: VS Code + virtual environment
  • Hardware: Regular laptop (no special hardware needed)


Instead of just showing raw satellite data, we created a complete beginner-friendly pipeline that turns three different satellite products into one unified, interactive experience. The combination of automatic data harmonization + map + burning-activity calendar + sensor comparison in a single simple web app is what makes the solution creative and practical for non-experts.

  • Accessibility for beginners (many NASA tools feel too complex)
  • Using only free and open data and tools
  • Focusing on a real geographic region (India) with multi-year data
  • Keeping the solution lightweight so it runs on ordinary computers
  • Making the app useful both for quick visual exploration and for downloading clean data for research
